label: requires minimum node count
type: DATATYPE PROPERTY: the subject service, feature or cluster behaviour requires at least N nodes. Object is an integer literal, not a concept id.
aliases_note: Round 26's general-settings.md extraction used BOTH spellings on the same page for the same thing - `requiresMinimumNodeCount` for auto-failover's three-node minimum and `hasMinimumNodeCount` elsewhere on the same form. A synonym fork that --variants cannot see, because the two names share no spelling to be a variant of: `requires`/`has` is a different WORD, not different punctuation. Folded here; the surviving name is the one already promoted. Union is 6 files, not 7 - the folded spelling's only file is one the surviving spelling already covers, which is the same-page evidence stated as a number. The subject scope is widened in the type field to match the evidence - auto-failover is a cluster behaviour, not a service - which is a correction to round 11's wording, not a new claim.
note: One of round 11's first datatype properties - see has-internal-service-identifier for why that distinction matters and was previously impossible to express.
relates_to_competency_question: How many nodes must run this service?
